 (By Kanikyamery, Advocate)
 :J U D G M E N T: 
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking
compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident. 
2. The case of the pet itioner is as follows: That on 31012017 at about 0710 p.m., the petitioner was standing at the left side of road waiting for Auto Rickshaw near Anjeneya Swamy Temple Bychapura Road, Devanahalli Taluk Town, at that time Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA43R 5341 which came from Devanahalli side with very high speed, rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner's, result of which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries on her face and leg. Immediately she was shifted to Akash Hospital at Devenahalli, where in it was diagnosed that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. She is still bedridden and as per advice of doctor, she is continuing her treatment till today. So far she has spent Rs.2, 00,000/ for her treatment. She was aged about 60 years; she was working as coolie and thereby earning Rs.8, 000/ per month. Due to permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work. She has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non pecuniary damages. 
3. Respondent No1 The IFFCO_TOKIO General Insurance Co.Ltd.,/insurer of two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA43R5341 has filed the written statement denied the averments of the petition. It is contended that there was delay of 01 day in lodging the compliant, thereafter false complaint was lodged by creating false story in order to get compensation. It is admitted by the respondent no 1 of the issuance of policy but their liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions. It is further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exaggerated, exorbitant speculative and unreasonable. It is further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner. As per the sketch the alleged accident has taken place 7 feet away from the mud footpath and it is clear that she stood on the road instead of mud footpath provided for the safety of the pedestrians and she has violated the traffic rules. It is further submitted that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle. With these averments the respondent no 1 has prayed to dismiss the petition. 
4. The respondent no 2 has filed written statement denying the manner of accident one stated by the petitioner. 
05. On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed. 
: I S S U E S:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Puttamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69541279/ 
2 Traffic Accident that occurred on 3101 2017 at about 0710 p.m., near Anjaneya Swamy Temple, Bychapura road, Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore District, due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA43R5341 by its rider as alleged? 
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award? 
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked in all 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14. On the other hand,
the respondent no.1 has examined its legal Assistant as RW.1 and got marked copy of policy as Ex.R3. During the crossexamination of PW.1 the learned counsel for the accused confronted the copy of Sketch and charge sheet and got marked as Ex.R.1 and 2 07. Heard arguments of the petitioner and respondents. The learned counsel for the petitioner has filed memo with citations as follows:
1. MFA No.2349/2022 dt 22112023:
Shri Lingaraju Vs. Yadukumar NH & Ors.,
2. LAWS (SC) 2018 , 20: Pappu Vs., Vinod Kumar Lamba 3. (2018) 9 SCC 650: Shamanna & Anr., Vs. Divisonal Manager, Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., & Ors.,
8. The learned counsel for the respondent no.2 has filed memo with ruling reported in Miscl.First Appeal No.200517 of 2019 (MVD). Perused the materials placed on record. 
9. My findings on the abovereferred Issues are as under: Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2: In Partly Affirmative. 
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following. 
:REASONS:
10. Issue No.1 :  In order to explain the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed her affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place 31012017 at about 710 p.m., when as pedestrian she was standing near Anjenya Swamy Temple,
Bychapura, Devanahalli Taluk and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by its rider. P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained,
treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
Puttamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69541279/
3 11. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of offending vehicle , P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 4 and 8 which are the police records such as F.I.R., FIS, MLC Intimation, IMV report, wound certificate, etc.
12. The respondents no 1 has seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioner and submitted that the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and that negligence was contributed solely by the petitioner who while standing in the middle of the road waiting for autorickshaw met with an accident. 
13. In the light of the defence taken by the respondent no.1, if the evidence of PW.1, complaint, spot mahazar with sketch is perused, though in the complaint it is stated that petitioner was standing by the side of road waiting to board the vehicle but in the evidence, the Pw1 herself has admitted that the accident in question has occurred at a distance of 7 feet from the left edge of tar road and that there was no zebra crossing. Though, the petitioner has produced spot mahazar but she has not produced the rough sketch for the reason best known to her. It is RW.1 who has produced the rough sketch and marked it as Ex.R1 through Pw1. If spot mahazar and rough sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot is nearly 20 feet and the spot of accident is at a distance of nearly 7 feet from the left edge of road towards right side. It is admitted by PW.1 that there was no zebra crossing near the spot of accident and that she was waiting for vehicle by standing on the tar road and that it was night hour and she has eye sight problems. When as per the own case of the petitioner, she was waiting for vehicle, she could have waited for vehicle by standing in the mud foot path provided for the safety of the pedestrian but the petitioner by violating the traffic rules and regulations stood on the road instead of mud foot path. Further on e cannot dispute that it is a busy road and number of vehicle are plying in the said road. Hence, the pedestrian have to stand in the foot path but not in the tar road. If petitioner was little bit cautious this accident could have been avoided. At the same time when it is a straight road, had the rider of the motorcycle ride his vehicle with moderate speed with all care and caution, he could have noticed the pedestrian standing in the road and at that time he could have avoided the accident by applying break. Hence both petitioner and rider of the offending vehicle have contributed negligence. Now at this juncture, it would be relevant to refer here the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 reported in ILR 1987 Karnataka page 2730 between Sharada Bai Vs. KSRTC., it is held that :
"A driver, particularly of a publictransport vehicle, is expected to have a proper look out and provide for the safety of the other users of the road. In a busy city, a driver must anticipated and provided for the more common follies of other users of the road. In crowded city roads it is not un often that pedestrians dart across the road,
cyclist and scooterists attempt to weave a zigzag path between other moving vehicles; school children who are left to fend for themselves, cross the streets unmindful of the hazards of traffic; and all these are a part of the realities of the urban predicament, which any driver, more particularly of a public transport system,
ought to be cognizant of. He must keep his anticipatory reflexes geared to be able to stop the vehicle at a very shortnotice. Roads are not meant only for heavyvehicles;
they are also meant for other users of the road and the drivers of heavyvehicles must negotiate their vehicles in such a way as not to jeopardise the safety of the other users Puttamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69541279/
4 of the road". 
"If the tortfeasor's negligence or breach of duty is established as causative of the damage, the onus is on him to establish that the victim's contributory negligence was a substantial or cooperating cause. In order to establish the defence of contributory negligence the propounder of that defence must prove, first, that the victim failed to take reasonable care of himself or, in other words, such care as a man of ordinary prudence would have done and that was a contributory cause of the accident. The amount of care which a person could reasonably be expected to take,
must needs vary with the circumstances and conditions actually prevailing at the material point of time. However, it is relevant to note that, in order to discharge of burden of proof, it is unnecessary for the propounder of that defence to adduce evidence about the matter. Contributory negligence can be and very often is inferred from the evidence already adduced on the claimants behalf or from the perceptive facts, either admitted or found established, on a balance of probabilities in the case". 
14. In unreported judgment rendered in MFA No. 7070/2015 (MV) between Smt.Mina Limbu &
Ors., Vs., M/s Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd., it was held by referring the facts of the case that "pedestrian crossing the road at a point where he ought not to have done, it has to be considered that pedestrian too has contributed negligence. In the said case, 25% of negligence was attributed against the deceased. 
15. In MFA NO.2380/2016 between Smt. Gangamma Vs., Sri. Vardharaju & Anr., in the said case also referring some of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it has observed that "where the person is crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing and accident occurs,
some percentage of negligence has to be attributed against the person who crossed the road and met with an accident". In the said case, 20% negligence was attributed against the deceased. 
16. Further in MFA No.2613/2010 Smt.N.Bharathamma & Ors., Vs. Mr.Syed Masood Matheen &
Anr., in the said case also by observing that deceased has contributed 25% to the occurrence and in the said case also the deceased while crossing the road had met with an accident.
17. Considering the materials placed on record so also the observation made in the aforesaid rulings,
since petitioner too has contributed negligence by standing in the road waiting for autorickshaw,
this court fixes the percentage of negligence on petitioner to an extent of 20%. Hence, the petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent 20% out of total compensation for the negligence contributed by her. Accordingly I answer issue no2 in Partly Affirmative. 
18. Issue No.2: The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustaining grievous injuries. 
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P5 and ExP.8. On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 31012017 to 15022017 at Akasha Institute of Medical Sciences & Research Centre,
Devanahalli, for a period of 16 days and underwent surgery for CRIF with INILN on 01022016. 
Puttamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69541279/
5 As per wound certificate the petitioner has sustained 3 injuries of which 2 injuries are grievous in nature. 
19. Dr.Ramesh B  Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore has given evidence as Pw3 and produced OPD book and Xrays at Ex.P.13 and 14. P.W.3 has deposed that the petitioner has sustained Grade II open left tibia fracture with no DNVD. PW.2 further deposed that he recently examined the petitioner on 16122023 for assessing the disability and further deposed that the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 26% of left lower limb which is 13% on whole body. 
20. During the cross examination, it is admitted by PW.3 that he has not treated the petitioner. It is admitted by PW.3 that he has assessed only the physical disability but not functional disability. 
21. Keeping in mind the evidence given by the PW.2, though he has stated that petitioner has sustained 13% of permanent disability on whole body but this court cannot accept it as gospel truth. 
Hence, this court inclines to take 10% as permanent disability on whole body instead of 13%.
22. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, and this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads. 
23. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries. Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/ towards pain and suffering. 
24. So far as medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, she has produced 29 medical bills for Rs.35,343/ at Ex.P.7. Hence this court inclines to award compensation under the medical head to the tune of Rs.35,343/.
25. It is stated that petitioner was 60 years and she was doing coolie, thereby earning Rs.8,000/
p.m. In order to substantiate the said contention though the petitioner has not produced any materials but considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner this court considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.8,000/ p.m.
26. The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 16 days as inpatient at Akasha Institute of Medical Sciences & Research Centre, Devanahalli. Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period. Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for three months. Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.24,000/ towards loss of income during the laid down period. 
27. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times. Further for 16 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to Puttamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69541279/
6 hospital for treatment. He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/ taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2017. 
28. The petitioner has contended that she is aged about 60 years as on the date of accident. 
Petitioner has produced Ex.P9/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows her date of birth as 01 011956 that means she was aged 61 years. Hence considering the Aadhar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 61 years. 
29. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.8, 000/ p.m and if 8% of loss of earning capacity i.e., 1/3rd on whole body is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 61 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 61 to 65 is '7'. So by applying the multiplier '7' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.53,760 /. Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.53,760/ (i.e., 8,000x8%x7x12 ) towards future loss of income due to disability. 
30. The petitioner at his age of 61 years has suffered two grievous injuries and permanent disability of 10%. Hence it may cause some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort. Hence this court inclines to award sum of Rs.15,000/ under the head loss of amenities and discomfort. The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
Sl. No Heads Amount Rs.
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs.50,000/
2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs.20,000/
 charges and nourishing food 3. Towards loss of income during Rs.24,000/
 laid up period 4. Loss of Future Income Rs.53,760 /
5. Medical bills Rs.35,343/
6. loss of comfort and amenities Rs.15,000/ 
 TOTAL Rs.1,98,103/ 
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,98,103 / (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Eight Thousand One Hundred and Three only).
31. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident. If the documents are perused, the rider of the offending vehicle was holding Learners License and it was issued on 31122016. The Learners License is valid up to 6 months. The permanent license should be applied for after 30 days and before 6 months from the date of issuance of the Learners License. In the present case,
admittedly the accident in question has taken place on 31012017 and Learners License was issued Puttamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69541279/
7 on 31122016 hence, it is within one month from the date of issuance Learners License, the present accident has occurred. 
32. Leaner's license is issued in Form No 3 under Rules 3 and 13 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989. Rule 3 authorizes the person holding learner's license to drive the vehicle subject to certain conditions as under:
3: General : The provisions of sub section (1) of section 3 shall not apply to a person while receiving instructions or gaining experience in driving with the object of presenting himself for a test of competence to drive so long as (a) ...............
(b) such person is accompanied by an instructor holding an effective driving license to drive the vehicle and such instructor is sitting in such a position to control or stop the vehicle.
33. It is clear from the aforesaid provisions that a person holding of learners license is authorized to drive the vehicle in any public place if such person is accompanied by an instructor holding an effective driving license to drive the vehicle and such instructors is sitting in such a position to control or stop the vehicle. The object being to gain experience in driving with a view to present himself for a test of competent to drive. 
34. In a ruling relied by the learned counsel for the respondent no 3 reported in 1996(2) SCC 328 (New India Assurance Co: Ltd / Mandar Madhav and others) and In ILR 2015 KAR 4490 between (Smt Asha Datt / The New India Assurance Co: Ltd and Another), where in also it was clearly observed that " A person holding learner's license is authorized to drive the vehicle in any public place if such person is accompanied by an instructor holding an effective driving license to drive the vehicle and such instructor is sitting in such a position to control or stop the vehicle. 
35. Coming to the case in hand, at the time of accident respondent no.2 alone was riding the vehicle and there was no one riding in the offending vehicle along with respondent no.1 holding valid driving license as pillion rider or as an instructor. Hence, it can be said without any hesitation that respondent no.2 rode the offending vehicle in the absence of instructor as instructor was not sitting behind her as pillion rider so as to control the vehicle in needy time and thereby respondent no.2 has violated Rule 3 of the Motor Vehicle Rules. So far as fixation of liability for violating the policy condition by driving his vehicle without having valid driving license is concerned, at this juncture it would be opt refer here the following rulings:
1. AIR 2018 SC 3726 Shamanna and Another / Divisional Manager Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others 2. AIR 2018 SC 2662 - Amrit Paul Singh and another / TATAAIG General Insurance Company Limited and Others Puttamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69541279/
8 3. AIR 2018 SC 4252 - Shivaraj / Rajendra and Another 36. In the aforesaid case though driver had no valid driving license and though vehicle had no permit and though claimant travelled in the tractor as passenger, the Hon'ble Apex court has confirmed the order of pay and recovery passed by the tribunal. 
37. Further learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2349/2022 (MVI): Shri Lingaraju Vs., Yadukumar N.H Vs. Anr., wherein the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving license but the Hon'ble High Court has directed the Insurance Company has deposit the compensation and to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle. 
38. In LAWS (SC) 2018 1 20: Civil Appeal No.20962/2017 :Pappu Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba. In the said case, applying the dictum in the case of National Insurance Company Swaran Singh has directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount in the first instance with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law. 
39. As insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident, the respondent no.1 is directed to pay the awarded amount and then to recover the amount from the respondent no.2. The awarded amount carries interest at the rate of 6 % p.a. Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered. 
40. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order. 
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs. 
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation Rs.1,98,103/ (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Eight Thousand One Hundred and Three only ). 
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay 80% compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.1,58,483/ and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award and to recover the said amount from the respondent no.2/owner of the offending vehicle. 
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit. 
Petitioner shall forgo 20% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.39,620/.
On deposit entire amount along with interest is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

"If the tortfeasor's negligence or breach of duty is established as causative of the damage, the onus is on him to establish that the victim's contributory negligence was a substantial or cooperating cause.

In order to establish the defence of contributory negligence the propounder of that defence must prove, first, that the victim failed to take reasonable care of himself or, in other words, such care as a man of ordinary prudence would have done and that was a contributory cause of the accident.

The amount of care which a person could reasonably be expected to take,
must needs vary with the circumstances and conditions actually prevailing at the material point of time.
However, it is relevant to note that, in order to discharge of burden of proof, it is unnecessary for the propounder of that defence to adduce evidence about the matter.

Contributory negligence can be and very often is inferred from the evidence already adduced on the claimants behalf or from the perceptive facts, either admitted or found established, on a balance of probabilities in the case".
